To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermodynamics of a system of particles with finite widths is described by the Fermi/Bose functions, rather than by the complicated combinations of the real and imaginary parts.

the thermodynamic functions for systems of particles with widths can always be expressed via the spectral function and Fermi–Bose distributions, and the thermodynamic consistency conditions are fulfilled.

1) Thermodynamically consistent approximate description of systems with particles with widths and quasiparticles can be constructed, 2) The interaction between species can be treated perturbatively and, 3) The system of fermions with widths and boson quasiparicles can be described by the ideal gas of fermion blurs interacting with bosons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a generalization of thermodynamics of systems with a finite number of particle species to the case when some of these species can be treated as particles with finite width.
the thermodynamic description of systems with resonances.
the thermodynamics of systems with finite mass-width.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system under study is a quasi-ideal gas of quasiparticles and blurs, where quasiparticle and blur contributions to the energy, entropy, etc., can be treated independently.
the thermodynamical consistency condition is fulfilled for a wide class of systems of particles and quasiparticles.
the thermodynamic properties of the system are not affected by the interaction between the fermions and the bosons, but only by the presence of the fermions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermodynamical consistency of the quasiparticles approximation can be achieved by a suitable choice of the spectral function, and that the interaction between species can be treated perturbatively in terms of the quasiboson–blur scattering amplitude.
thermodynamic consistency of a system of particles with finite widths can be fulfilled, provided spectral functions are known.
a thermodynamic treatment of a system of interacting particle species, each species with finite mass-width, is possible provided the spectral function of each species is known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermodynamical description of the system of resonant fermions interacting with boson quasifields is not much complicated than the description of a quasi-ideal gas of fermions and bosons.

thermodynamics of a system of particles with finite widths is described by the same expressions as the thermodynamics of the system of particles with zero width, if spectral functions of particle types are used instead of self-energies.

, in the case of a strong coupling between species, the thermodynamic properties of the system of particles with widths and quasiparticles are determined by the properties of the system with quasiparticles, and the contribution of particles with widths is suppressed.
